summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis and severe asthma was admitted after developing hypercarbic respiratory failure during an asthma exacerbation, requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. He was transferred to the ICU, where he was treated with sedation, paralysis, and antibiotics after bronchoscopy revealed influenza B, MSSA, and Serratia. He improved clinically, was successfully extubated, and transitioned to oral therapy. Imaging showed cirrhosis and a liver lesion requiring further evaluation with MRI. His home medications for cirrhosis and asthma were restarted. He was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with follow-up arranged for hepatology, pulmonology, and consideration of Xolair and sleep apnea evaluation.
